_comment: Difficulty presets (PLAN.md §7.6), chosen when a world is created: five hereditary titles, easiest first (Baron is the old Normal, Viscount the old Hard, Count the old Nightmare). `description` says in a line what the title means; the numbers are spelled out beside it in the game. Wave size = base size (waves.json) × waveScale × group power, kept between floor and maxFactor. Group power grows with powerWeight for every village beyond one per player, and for army strength above power.perPlayer per player, which itself grows by power.growthPerWave each wave. Army strength is the group's collective power, watched each time a horde is planned: every fighting unit it has (at home, in training, out in the field) counts its attack, defense and health, each times power.weights. campRate scales camps per wave (camps.json). Camps that rise after a wave (not those placed when the run starts) are as many more units bigger as group power makes waves (the same factor without waveScale and the floor, never below 1, at most maxFactor). fearWeight scales how much hordes heed fear (0: they don't learn). razeThreshold is added to the raze decision's threshold (lower razes sooner); graceWaves is how many waves only raid.

baron.name: Baron
baron.description: A border lord's charge: hordes come in their usual numbers and give you five quiet raids to dig in.

viscount.name: Viscount
viscount.description: Bigger hordes that keep pace with your strength, more camps, and only three raids before they come to burn.

count.name: Count
count.description: Hordes half again as large, camps everywhere, and no grace: the first horde may already burn a village.

marquess.name: Marquess
marquess.description: A march on the edge of Nav: huge hordes that grow as fast as you do, and burn rather than plunder.

duke.name: Duke
duke.description: The whole of Nav against your duchy: the largest hordes, the most camps, and no mercy at all.
